correspondence.component_scope: western headward feeder and Pearce Lake passage
correspondence.finding: The selected initial line follows mapped connected small lakes and the eastward stream valley into Pearce Lake. Its generalized passage through the southern lake arm corresponds to the same waterbody. The raster shows the connecting channels as well as adjoining tributaries; the initial point is a retained selection endpoint, not a claimed surveyed source.
correspondence.name_limit: Pearce Lake is a lake-component label; no hydronym is assigned to the headward feeder.
correspondence.correspondence: supported at ordinary generalized corridor scale

correspondence.finding: The source shows a continuous eastward watercourse through intervening small waterbodies to the southern Curtis Lake arm. The selected line then follows the elongated lake northward. Simplified corners differ from the mapped channel and shore curves, but no actual connector remains uncovered.
correspondence.name_limit: Mapped lake labels establish component identities, not a shared name for the interlake stream.
correspondence.correspondence: supported at ordinary generalized corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Curtis–Stewart connection and Stewart Lake passage
correspondence.finding: A narrow mapped stream connects the east side of Curtis Lake with Stewart Lake around the intervening upland. The selected line crosses this same connection and then follows Stewart Lake southward. The raster was inspected without the selected-line overlay at the narrow connector.
correspondence.correspondence: supported at ordinary generalized corridor scale

correspondence.finding: The raster shows the Stewart outlet stream becoming braided before entering the adjoining lake complex, then the connected water passages eastward and southeastward through Qamanialuk Lakes. These include the material junctions and small connections crossed by the selected generalized line. The distinct CGM204 online description separately corroborates the Stewart-to-Qamanialuk connection.
correspondence.name_limit: No name is assigned to the outlet stream merely from the names of its connected lakes.
correspondence.correspondence: supported at ordinary generalized corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: lower valley bends and coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The source shows the same connected lower stream and lake valleys around the intervening uplands, including the broad return bend and final coastward branch. The terminal lies in a mapped river-mouth setting with coastal shoal/intertidal symbols. The source channel connections, nearby tributary junctions and final shoreward connection were inspected directly. No exact active branch, current flow direction at each minor junction, tidal boundary, bank or surveyed mouth vertex is asserted.
correspondence.name_limit: The label Ikkattujuq appears beside a lower lake-linked section, but its formal extent and feature-type scope are not established here. It is not adopted as a river or whole-system name.
correspondence.correspondence: supported at ordinary generalized corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern headward and upper westward corridor
correspondence.finding: The original headward view shows a linked sequence of narrow channels and small waterbody expansions matching the selected upper westward course, its broad northern bend and southwestward continuation. Readable Isortoq River labels occur along this connected channel. At Causeway Lake, the original shows the adjoining lake connection and the continuing main channel; the generalized selection is not treated as a precise traverse of that small lake.
correspondence.limits: Names for the individual small headward lakes and exact initial reach remain null; no natural source point is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward middle bend and glacier-side joining setting
correspondence.finding: The selected southwest approach leads to the broad turn into the southward valley. The map continuously shows the trunk and tributaries joining from the west/north and from the Barnes Ice Cap side. Downstream, the route bends beside the Lewis Glacier setting and continues through a broadened, islanded river corridor toward the Limit Lake vicinity. The source view covers the actual connections rather than relying on ice-cap proximity or a regional name label.
correspondence.limits: The journal describes Rimrock River joining the upper bend and two glacier-side tributaries farther down; exact selected confluence vertices and every tributary name are not assigned. Flitaway Lake and Lewis Glacier are adjoining context.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward middle trunk to Isortoq Lake inlet
correspondence.finding: The source maps show the same southwest and west course through the islanded/braided reach, subsequent narrower channel bends, material northern/southern joining streams and the turn toward the northeast end of Isortoq Lake. The Limit Lake vicinity is visible; its local label is not promoted to a precisely bounded selected-lake assignment. River labels continue along the trunk.
correspondence.limits: Generalized bends are compared by their connected valley sequence, not by bank coincidence. Nearby tributary lakes are not substituted for the mainstem.

correspondence.component_scope: Isortoq Lake passage, lower river and fiord terminal
correspondence.finding: The overlapping lake and terminal views show the river entering the northeastern end of Isortoq Lake, the continuous elongated southwestward lake passage, its southwestern outlet and the lower river turning south toward the fiord head. The lower channel and terminal setting remain connected in the original cartography. The overview supplies the Isortoq Fiord label.
correspondence.limits: Isortoq Lake retains its lake identity. No exact branch, bank, contemporary tidal transition or surveyed mouth point is selected.

correspondence.component_scope: Initial unnamed feeder and westward connection
correspondence.finding: The detailed original map shows a small-lake and stream drainage from the eastern beginning running southwest and west through a shallow valley into the broader Murchison River corridor. The selected display loop is strongly generalized relative to the mapped stream bends. The connection is visible as mapped watercourse continuity rather than inferred from proximity of a name label.
correspondence.name_limit: No readable hydronym establishes a separate name for the initial feeder or lake. Murchison River labels on the receiving trunk are not extended automatically to this feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeast trunk and eastward middle bend
correspondence.finding: Repeated Murchison River labels occur on the broad braided valley followed northeast by the selection, around the eastward middle bend, and on the northward reach approaching the lake. The map shows the connected valley and broad bend continuously across overlapping views. Darby Lake is a separate nearby southern waterbody rather than a selected crossing.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported representative trunk and complete middle geographic corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Murchison Lake and northern river continuation
correspondence.finding: The selected northeastward broad-water passage follows the elongated waterbody repeatedly labeled Murchison Lake. Its northeastern outlet continues through the mapped Murchison River, including narrower channel sections, a northern bend and the broad westward river reach. The lake-to-river connections are visible in the original map.
correspondence.name_limit: Murchison Lake remains a separately named waterbody. Murchison River labels resume on the connected outlet corridor; no exact legal name-transition vertex is assigned.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete lake crossing and channel connections supported.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward lower river and Inglis Bay terminal
correspondence.finding: The source follows the Murchison River west through widened channel reaches and then northwest into a broad wetland and branching coastal tract. Multiple channels reach Inglis Bay around the mapped Avalliq Island and Kuungmiuvik Island setting. The selected generalized end belongs to this terminal complex; it is not treated as an exact present-day distributary trace or surveyed mouth. ARC403 chapter 8, printed page 8-7, paragraph 125 independently places Murchison River and Inglis River on the east side of Inglis Bay.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported through the broad actual coastal terminal; no material connector gap.

correspondence.finding: The retained opening descends southeast on the Grande-side drainage east of Ejutla, continues through the San Diego-side joining corridor and Peña Larga, then follows the eastward low bend toward the San Luis Amatlán-side junction setting. The neighboring Atoyac/Coapa route to the west and the separate San Juan approach are not substituted for this selection.
correspondence.limits: The exact first modeled reach name and Grande/San Diego/Peña Larga transition vertices are not assigned.

correspondence.finding: The selected route turns northeast and north through the Río Seco/Santa María Zoquitlán setting toward San Pedro Totolápam, then follows the eastward valley past the La Mancornada/Las Ánimas setting to the Nejapa approach. The full connecting course is visible on the state original.
correspondence.limits: Settlement names orient the selected watercourse and are not asserted as hydronyms. Unlabeled or unresolved local reach names remain unassigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern loop and eastern middle corridor
correspondence.finding: From the Nejapa setting the selected river turns north toward Guadalupe Lachiriega/Santo Domingo Narro, then east and southeast through the Shilabala joining setting. It continues down the valley toward Arroyo las Truchas and the northern arm of Presidente Benito Juárez. This distinctive northward loop and southeast continuation match the complete retained middle course.
correspondence.limits: Neighboring branches near Santa Ana Tavela, Santiago Lachiguiri and the Tequisistlán valley are context, not additional selected rivers.

correspondence.finding: The selected northern incoming trunk is directly labeled Tehuantepec in the Jalapa original and passes through the Presidente Benito Juárez reservoir setting to its southeast outlet. The route then continues east and southeast toward Santa María Mixtequilla and Santo Domingo Tehuantepec. The separately named Tequisistlán approach enters from the west and is not the selected upstream route.
correspondence.limits: The modeled reservoir crossing is assessed as component/corridor correspondence. A different reservoir centerline or historical shoreline does not establish a material geographic gap or a name change.

correspondence.finding: The selected channel continues southeast from Santo Domingo Tehuantepec/San Blas Atempa through San Pedro Huilotepec, where the municipal original directly labels it Tehuantepec. The state sheet continues this same channel to the Pacific shore by Boca del Río and Ensenada de la Ventosa in the Gulf of Tehuantepec setting. Nearby Laguna Superior, Huazantlán del Río waterways and Salina Cruz harbor are distinct coastal context.
correspondence.limits: No exact bank, mouth vertex, present flow or shoreline intersection is asserted; the review covers the ordinary generalized terminal corridor.
